segments.caption: The video opens with a GMC Certified Service title card introducing the topic: "Replacing Your Tires." A technician, wearing a branded shirt, then appears in front of a blue backdrop alongside a dark blue GMC pickup truck, setting the stage for a professional, step-by-step guide on tire replacement for GMC vehicles.
A GMC Certified Service representative, Dave Campbell, stands in front of a dark blue GMC Sierra pickup truck, speaking directly to the camera in a studio setting with a blue curtain backdrop.
A GMC service technician demonstrates the process of changing a tire on a vehicle, shown in a split-screen format with close-ups of the wheel and the mechanic's hands working on the lug nuts.

A mechanic is shown installing a tire on a vehicle in a garage, while a GMC service representative speaks to the camera in front of a GMC truck, highlighting professional vehicle maintenance and service.

A GMC service representative stands before a dark blue GMC pickup truck, introducing a segment on tire tread condition. The video then transitions to a split-screen comparison, clearly illustrating the difference between "Good Tread" and "Bad Tread" on vehicle tires.

The segment presents a side-by-side visual comparison of tire tread conditions, labeled "Good Tread" and "Bad Tread," to illustrate the difference in wear. A text overlay then appears, stating "GMC Recommends Rotating Tires Every 7,500 Miles," directly linking the visual example to a specific maintenance recommendation for vehicle owners.

This segment visually explains tire maintenance by first contrasting “Good Tread” and “Bad Tread” to illustrate wear, then demonstrating how to measure tread depth using a specialized gauge, all under the consistent recommendation that tires should be rotated every 7,500 miles.
A hand uses a tire tread depth gauge and then a penny to measure the tread depth on a car tire, demonstrating how to check if the tire is worn.

A GMC service technician demonstrates how to check for tire tread wear by using a penny. He presses the coin into the tire's tread, and a red arrow graphic highlights the measurement, indicating that if the top of Lincoln’s head is visible, the tread is too shallow and the tire needs to be replaced.

A GMC service technician speaks to the camera in front of a dark blue GMC Sierra pickup truck, introducing a topic related to vehicle maintenance. The scene then cuts to a close-up shot of a mechanic using a wrench to tighten a bolt on a vehicle's wheel hub assembly, illustrating a specific repair or service procedure.

A close-up view shows a mechanic using a wrench to tighten or loosen a bolt on the exhaust system near the wheel hub of a car elevated on a lift. The camera slowly pans and zooms out, revealing the shiny, multi-spoke alloy wheel as the focus shifts from the exhaust pipe to the wheel's center, highlighting the ongoing mechanical work in a garage setting.

A GMC service technician speaks to the camera in front of a dark blue GMC truck, introducing a topic related to vehicle maintenance. The segment cuts to close-up shots of a wheel hub being worked on and a damaged concrete curb, illustrating potential causes or consequences of tire damage or road hazards.

A GMC service technician speaks to the camera in front of a dark blue GMC Sierra pickup truck, likely introducing or explaining a topic related to vehicle maintenance or repair, as suggested by the first frame's close-up of a cracked and damaged road surface, which may be the subject of his discussion.

A GMC Certified Service representative speaks to the camera in front of a dark blue GMC truck, introducing the brand's certified service program. The video then transitions to show the exterior of a "Certified Service" dealership sign, followed by a scene inside the service center where two female staff members are assisting a customer with a vehicle, illustrating the hands-on, customer-focused nature of the service experience.

A GMC Certified Service technician speaks directly to the camera in a studio setting, with a black GMC Sierra truck prominently displayed behind him. The scene is framed by a lower-third graphic displaying the GMC logo and the website gmccertifiedservice.com, indicating a promotional or informational segment about GMC vehicle service.

A GMC Certified Service technician speaks directly to the camera in a studio setting, with a dark GMC truck visible behind him. The video introduces the topic "Replacing Your Tires" as part of the GMC Certified Service program, concluding with a branded title card and a black screen.
